Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain. The reported injury is
consistent with the mechanism and force of the impact. Over the course of care, the patient completed 24 visits, a somewhat
longer course than typically expected for a cervical and lumbar strain. Examination documented paraspinal muscle tenderness
and reduced cervical range of motion, supporting the presence of soft tissue injury, while neurological screening, straight leg
raise, and reflex testing returned normal results. No prior injury or treatment involving the neck or low back is known to this
provider. Records review identified a duplicate charge for one date of service; the rendering provider acknowledged that the
second entry was a repeat billing and that it does not reflect a separate visit. Treatment included manual therapy, therapeutic
exercise, and home exercise instruction, with gradual improvement noted. Continued self-directed rehabilitation and follow-up as
needed are recommended.
